problem.text: Let $ABCDEF$ be a regular hexagon with side length $1$. Denote by $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ the midpoints of sides $\overline{AB}$, $\overline{CD}$, and $\overline{EF}$, respectively. What is the area of the convex hexagon whose interior is the intersection of the interiors of $\triangle ACE$ and $\triangle XYZ$?

steps.title: Where to start: a triangle with its corners cut off
steps.body: The overlap of two triangles is hard to measure directly, so start from one whole triangle and remove what sticks out. Each corner of $\triangle XYZ$ is the midpoint of a hexagon side, and it lies outside $\triangle ACE$, past one of its sides (for example $X$ lies past side $AC$). So the hexagon is $\triangle XYZ$ with three small corner triangles cut off, and by symmetry all three are the same size.

your_turn.prompt: Why are both triangles equilateral? Think about turning the hexagon by $120^\circ$ about its center.
your_turn.answer: The turn sends $A\to C\to E$ and $X\to Y\to Z$, so each triangle is carried onto itself and all its sides are equal.

steps.title: The area of $\triangle XYZ$
steps.body: The center $O$ of the hexagon is at distance $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ from every side's midpoint (that is the height of one of the six equilateral triangles of side $1$ that make up the hexagon). $X$ and $Y$ are $120^\circ$ apart around $O$, and a triangle with two sides $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and a $120^\circ$ angle between them has third side $\sqrt3$ times as long. So $XY=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot\sqrt3=\frac32$.

your_turn.prompt: An equilateral triangle of side $s$ has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2$. Find the area of $\triangle XYZ$.

steps.title: Measure the corner at $X$
steps.body: Line $AC$ cuts off the corner at $X$, crossing $XY$ and $XZ$. Put the center at the origin with $A=(1,0)$ and $C=\left(-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)$; then $X=\left(\frac34,\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\right)$ and line $AC$ is $x+\sqrt3\,y=1$. Side $XY$ is horizontal, and line $AC$ cuts $XZ$ at distance $\frac14$ from $X$. Careful: the corner triangle is not equilateral, because its two sides at $X$ have different lengths.

your_turn.prompt: $XY$ lies on the line $y=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$. Where does it meet line $AC$, and how far is that from $X$?
your_turn.answer: At $x=1-\frac34=\frac14$, so the distance from $X$ is $\frac34-\frac14=\frac12$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Each corner triangle has sides $\frac12$ and $\frac14$ with a $60^\circ$ angle between them, so its area is $\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac14\cdot\sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{32}$. Removing three of them:
$$\frac{9\sqrt3}{16}-3\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{32}=\frac{18\sqrt3-3\sqrt3}{32}=\frac{15}{32}\sqrt3.$$
The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.E: $\frac{9}{16}\sqrt3$ is the area of the whole triangle $XYZ$. Its three corners stick out past triangle $ACE$ and must be cut off.
wrong_choices.A: $\frac38\sqrt3$ comes from assuming the cut-off corners are equilateral with side $\frac12$ (or that the hexagon is regular). The corners actually have sides $\frac12$ and $\frac14$ at $X$, and the hexagon's sides alternate $\frac34$ and $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$.
